data.title: ‘The big advantage for us lies in flexibility’ – Electra manager Paul Tonini on battery storage
data.description: Electra is increasingly relying on battery storage systems for its fast-charging parks. In Germany alone, 20 storage systems are already installed, and this number is expected to reach around 40 by the end of the year. In this interview, Germany CEO Paul Tonini explains the advantages of the technology, why grid operators sometimes complicate its deployment, and why battery storage alone cannot solve the challenges of expanding the charging network.

data.title: Envoy and LACI launch EV car-sharing initiative in New Jersey
data.description: The partners will deploy up to 30 shared EVs in Hudson and Bergen counties. An $8.5 million (around €7.8 million) state grant funds the project to expand electric mobility in underserved communities.

data.title: Mercedes receives KBA approval for door-to-door driving assistant
data.description: Mercedes-Benz has become the first automaker in Germany to receive regulatory approval for a point-to-point driving assistant. The German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) approved the MB.Drive Assist Pro system based on UN Regulation R171. This enables automated door-to-door driving at SAE Level 2, including complex urban traffic situations.

data.title: Siemens introduces DC contactor for megawatt charging
data.description: Siemens is expanding its DC portfolio with a high-performance DC contactor for voltages up to 1,500 volts and currents up to 600 amperes. The new SIRIUS 3QC1 combines semiconductor technology with mechanical contacts and is intended for use in megawatt charging stations for commercial vehicles.

data.title: Court deems BYD Ti7 too similar to JLR Defender
data.description: A Dutch court has ordered ten BYD subsidiaries in interim proceedings to refrain from building and selling the Ti7 in the EU. According to the judges, the model looks too similar to the JLR Defender. However, the main trial is still pending.

data.title: Zenobē expands into Germany
data.description: British commercial fleet electrification specialist Zenobē is bringing its offerings to Germany. Zenobē provides fleet operators with a fixed-price solution that includes EVs, charging infrastructure, battery management, and fleet management software.

data.title: TruckCharge Network now integrates public chargers from Milence
data.description: Daimler Truck reports that its TruckCharge network now covers 21 markets and has recently integrated Milence's charging points. The initiative began in 2025 as a semi-public electric truck charging network with locations at dealers and customers. In addition to depot chargers, the integration of public chargers is also becoming increasingly important.

data.title: VW ID. Polo: customers now face year-long wait times
data.description: Volkswagen has apparently significantly underestimated the success of its new electric small car family. Customers for the VW ID. Polo sometimes have to wait more than a year, and the other three models also require a lot of patience. Now, production in Spain is to be scaled up more quickly. However, a shortage of battery cells is also slowing down production.

data.title: Onsemi introduces new SiC Platform: EliteSiC M4
data.description: US semiconductor manufacturer Onsemi has introduced the fourth generation of its silicon carbide technology with EliteSiC M4. The new platform is set to increase power density by up to 30 per cent and reduce losses by up to 35 per cent. This could benefit, among other things, the drivetrain systems of electric vehicles.

data.title: Solaris delivers 13 hydrogen buses to France
data.description: Solaris has delivered thirteen Urbino 12 hydrogen buses to the Béziers Méditerranée community association in southern France. In future, the vehicles will be used by the beeMob local transport network.

data.title: Adani Cement to deploy 410 heavy-duty electric trucks
data.description: Indian cement manufacturer Adani Cement (Adani Group) has announced plans to add 410 heavy-duty electric trucks to its fleet. It has already flagged off the first batch as part of the initiative and will commission the remaining trucks by March 2027.

data.title: Alpitronic builds DC fast charger factory in South Carolina, USA
data.description: Alpitronic is expanding its presence in the USA and investing nearly US$34 million in its own production facility for fast-charging stations in South Carolina. Additionally, the South Tyrolean charging infrastructure specialist is strengthening its North America management with Christopher Balcom as the new Chief Commercial Officer.

data.title: Aachen startup Cylib acquires BASF’s battery recycling business
data.description: In a major development for what is a relatively young company, Aachen-based battery recycling startup Cylib is taking over BASF's mucbh battery recycling business. The deal includes, among other things, two facilities in Schwarzheide (Brandenburg) and the North America business.

data.title: Opel and Leapmotor formalise battery-electric SUV partnership
data.description: Opel and Leapmotor have officially agreed to collaborate on the development of a new electric SUV. With a launch date penned for 2028, the model will use key components from the Chinese manufacturer and will be produced at Stellantis' plant in Zaragoza, Spain.

data.title: EU-China hybrid import quota unlikely to apply to range extenders
data.description: The annual import quota of 350,000 hybrid vehicles agreed upon between the EU and China in October apparently does not include electric vehicles with range extenders. Instead, these cars are likely to continue being classified as battery-electric vehicles and thus be subject to the special tariffs on EVs, but no import quota would apply.

data.title: BMW iX4 rolls off production line alongside iX3 in Debrecen
data.description: Following the BMW iX3, series production of the BMW iX4 has now also begun at BMW's plant in Debrecen - making the new SUV, with its coupé silhouette, the second model of the Neue Klasse to be produced at the Hungarian BMW plant. The iX4 will reach dealers starting March 2027 - initially in two drivetrain variants.

data.title: Chinese electric SC01 sportscar to be built in Italy from May 2027
data.description: The company FIPA plans to establish a new production site for EVs in the Marken region of eastern Italy. From the end of May 2027, a Chinese electric sports car - the SC01 - will be assembled there. By 2030, the company aims to employ 285 people and later expand production to include light electric vehicles.

data.title: Lagos further expands electric bus fleet
data.description: Eleven new electric buses for public transport have been introduced in Lagos, Nigeria. The vehicles are from Oando Clean Energy and represent the first batch of a planned delivery of 50 electric buses. In the long term, 552 e-buses are to be deployed on the routes across the megacity.

data.title: VW to present battery-electric VW ID. Polo GTI concept – for the racetrack
data.description: A 240 km/h top speed and 0 to 100 km/h in 4.7 seconds: with the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, Volkswagen is demonstrating how the GTI idea can evolve in the electric age. The sprint-strong study delivers 270 kW - that's nearly 370 hp in old currency.

data.title: GTA VI fans praise lightning-fast EV charging speeds
data.description: The hype around Grand Theft Auto VI is enormous - and the automotive industry is getting heavily involved. BMW, Daimler Truck, and Sixt are using the game’s aesthetic for their social media presence. But electromobility also has its place in the game itself: in Vice City, charging EVs happens much faster than in real life.
